method: Independent review of data/latest.json, data/qa/briefs.json and data/videos.json only; no network access to the platforms, no video inspection (titles, creators, categories, statistics, dates and reasons as exposed by the system); docs/RECOMMENDATION_AUDIT.md and data/benchmark/audit-4.0.json were not read.

desk.name: Satisfying & ASMR
desk.notes: 3 of 6 evidence items are satisfying/ASMR shorts; 2 are ended livestream recordings (80-96 min, +2/h and +3/h, flagged cooling by the system) and 1 is a Hindi car-restoration short. "6 clean verified" counts the streams. Best example decelerating (0.53x lifetime) while timing says "emerging". Briefs propose dialogue/character comedy and a 93-173 s target derived from a median contaminated by the streams; the real shorts run 34-98 s.

desk.name: halloween
desk.notes: All evidence on-topic, calendar type correct, cross-platform (YouTube, Bluesky, Google Trends), top video genuinely accelerating (1.79x). But category is "Music / Covers & Mashups" (evidence is costumes, pet costumes, SFX makeup, decor), so the approach becomes "original parody track"; timing never states that the date is 3 days away; 3 of 6 examples are already cooling; sub-formats visible in the evidence (pet costume reveal, costume ranking "Part N", SFX makeup) are never named.

desk.name: Cooking & recipes
desk.notes: Evidence is AI dogs "cooking", two Hindi family-drama skits tagged #cooking, a cat video matched on the word "cook", and a rejected item; at most one is a recipe. The pool is flagged generic/unqualified at trend level yet reaches the desk. "Mostly English/Spanish" is false (romanised Hindi tagged "latin"/"en"). Briefs invent "a 60-second recipe" that no evidence shows.

desk.name: aianimation
desk.notes: "10 clean verified videos" vs 1 verified + 5 rejected in the evidence shown. 88% of attention is one Hindi car-transformation short whose link to #aianimation is not visible in its title (tags/descriptions are not stored). A medium hashtag labelled "event" with confidence 80. Briefs: "Aianimation, but something is wrong".

desk.name: Storytime & narration
desk.notes: Two verified couple-POV shorts (one 14.1M in 2 days) plus a rejected FIFA gaming video. "1 creator repeats the format" is impossible with 3 videos from 3 creators (it comes from the wider cluster). The strong example is a POV skit rather than narration. Briefs include "A 30-second original song about told story". Monitor is the right action.

desk.name: Puppet & character videos
desk.notes: "6 clean verified" vs 1 verified + 1 early + 4 rejected shown, including a 56-min horror game stream, two Jeff Dunham TV-clip reuploads and a Bluesky text post about a drug ad (0 views); the trend record also holds an ABC News sentencing clip. The 78%-dominant video is a Korean short with no puppet signal in its title. "Event" is a fallback for "one video dominates". Briefs recommend hashtagging a real comedian's name; no Content ID warning for the clip material.

A year token that appears in every trailer title (Avengers: Doomsday, Dune 3, Way of the Warrior Kid). Not a trend; should have been caught by the generic-token filter. Category "Music / Original Songs" drives "the 2026 song" brief with hashtags #2026 #trailer #chris #pratt. 4 of 6 examples are cooling (0.02-0.57x) while timing says "emerging". Monetization suggests streaming an original track about a year.

desk.name: mbappe
desk.notes: A real news moment (Ballon d'Or ceremony + El Clasico) typed correctly, but category "Animation & Art" while all 5 evidence items are Sports. topViews 2.18M although an evidence item shows 4.17M (dominance 53% is computed on a different set). Best example cooling at 0.15x lifetime; a ceremony that already happened is "emerging"/"monitor". feasibleIn2h is false (1.5-4 h) yet it sits on the desk and a brief says "Low" difficulty at 1.5-4 h. The visible owner-fit opportunity (AI 3D football parodies by several channels) is never named. No likeness/footage-rights note.

lane.notes: Honest about its limits (notes say "too broad", "did not clear the desk gate", "fewer than 3 clean verified examples") and it is the only view centred on the owner's pools, so it works as a watchlist. It does not work as a recommendation: 2-4 examples per pool, several off-pool (a brand's advert music video and a K-pop news short under "Music videos"; Talking Tom game streams under "Animal comedy"; a rejected how-to tutorial and a rejected 19K-view AI short as the entire "AI-generated video" pool while the trend list reports 26 creators / 29 videos for the same pool; a 3D-pen craft vlog under "Animation shorts"). "Animation shorts" (177 creators) is dismissed as category-level instead of being split into the sub-formats visible in its own examples (AI 3D football parody, 3D explainer).

strengths: Every card and brief carries plain-language reasons with the real numbers (views, age, age-specific hit floor, lifetime average vs measured rate, acceleration, creator baseline) and the briefs admit that visual style and audio were never inspected.

Growth is labelled honestly at the video level ("an average, not a measured recent rate", "provisional", acceleration only claimed on >=1,000 gained views) and the desk refuses to claim cluster growth without 24h of history.

The calendar event (halloween) is handled well: correct type, corroborated on three sources, "one piece before the date, not a series", with the collapse-after-the-date risk carried into the revenue section.
The desk gate publishes its exclusion reasons with counts, and the lane notes are candid about pools being too broad or too thin.
Monetization eligibility lines are accurate (YPP Shorts threshold, TikTok Creator Rewards >=1 min) and the "inauthentic content" warning is exactly the risk an AI-video creator faces.
weaknesses: Desk headline claims contradict the evidence shown: "N clean verified videos" while the evidence lists rejected items, two ended livestream recordings, a Bluesky text post, a news clip and TV reuploads (aianimation: "10 clean verified" vs 1 verified + 5 rejected).

Relevance matching is title-keyword only (tags and descriptions are empty in the index): "cook" pulls a cat video into Cooking, "satisfying" pulls a car restoration into ASMR, the year "2026" turns every trailer into a trend, "jeff dunham" clip reuploads define a "puppet format". Three of the eight desk items (2026, aianimation, Puppet & character videos) are not trends.

Timing is uninformative and sometimes inverted: all eight opportunities are "emerging" with timingScore 50 because the index itself is 8-11h old; in the same file the trend windows say "peaking" with measured growth; best examples that the system flags as cooling (mbappe 0.15x, 2026 0.22x, Satisfying 0.53x) are presented as "gaining +N/h"; the Halloween countdown and the already-held Ballon d'Or ceremony never enter the timing.

Category classification is wrong on 3 of 8 desk items (halloween -> Music, 2026 -> Music/Original Songs, mbappe -> Animation & Art) and the error propagates into the production approach ("original parody track") and monetization ("streams of the original track").

Briefs are five rotating templates with the trend name string-substituted ("An original recurring character takes on 2026 (trailer / chris)", "A 30-second original song about told story", "Aianimation, but something is wrong"); none is derived from the observed hooks or sub-formats, durations come from contaminated medians, and one desk item (mbappe) is over the 2h budget yet still briefed.

The opportunity-type classifier is weak outside "uncertain": 0/10 "meme" labels agreed (generic hashtags with 3-5 creators), "event" is a fallback for "one video dominates" and for description boilerplate ("Abonne Toi", "Get Ready"), and "format" is applied by construction to category pools the system itself marks generic (Cat videos, Dog videos, Gaming clips).

Early Radar is not early: 14/40 entries are older than 72h, 22/40 are decelerating (measured below lifetime average), 21/40 already have >=1M views; "the measured rate is abnormal" is printed for rates at 0.7-0.96x the video's own average because the rule is an absolute >=10K/h bar; #1 is a 4-day-old TV clip.

Feed hygiene: hashtag-only titles, identical-title multi-uploads from one channel, aggregator reposts, a 50-minute show episode and TV clips reach the top 10s; language detection labels romanised Hindi and French as "en"/"latin", so the "mostly English/Spanish" fit claim is false where it matters.

Numeric inconsistencies that an owner will notice: mbappe topViews 2.18M while an evidence item shows 4.17M; "1 creator repeats the format" on a 3-video / 3-creator cluster; a "Low difficulty" brief at 1.5-4h; the Satisfying median duration (133 s) computed with 80-96-minute streams.

The owner's own lane (AI video, animation, characters, music) is the weakest-served: the "AI-generated video" pool shows one rejected tutorial and one rejected 19K-view short while the trend list reports 26 creators; "Animation shorts" (177 creators) is dismissed as too broad instead of being split into the sub-formats visible in its own examples (AI 3D football parodies, 3D explainers), which would have been the single most owner-fit recommendation in this snapshot.
fixes: 1. Evidence integrity before anything else: count only what is shown; drop rejected, cooling-to-zero, livestream-recording, Bluesky-text and news items from "clean verified"; block generic tokens (years, "shorts", "viral", "fyp") and description boilerplate ("Abonne Toi", "Get Ready", "Fair Use", "Entertainment Purposes", "Auto Generated") before clustering; dedupe identical-title uploads per channel and hashtag-only titles in the feeds.

2. Fix relevance matching: store tags/description hashtags in the index, require the trend keyword or signature to appear in title or tags, show the matched term on every evidence card, and add negative rules (a "cook" match needs a food category; "satisfying" needs <=180 s and an ASMR/satisfying tag; a single dominant video must itself match the signature).

3. Redefine Early Radar as early: age <=48h (or <=72h with views below half the floor), measured rate >=1.5x the lifetime average over >=2h, views <1M, and no "abnormal" wording when the ratio is below 1; demote TV/show clips and channels with no upload history.

4. Derive category, production approach and timing from the evidence, not the taxonomy: majority platform category of the verified examples; calendar countdown for events (days to date, "already happened" for past ceremonies); cooling share and measured/lifetime ratio of the top examples in the timing label; reconcile desk growth ("not measurable") with the trend window ("measured, peaking") — one source of truth.

5. Replace template briefs with evidence-grounded ones: name the sub-format actually visible in the top three verified shorts (pet-costume reveal, costume ranking "Part N", AI 3D football parody), derive hook, beat sheet and duration from those shorts only (never from streams or long-form), keep the three variations but tie each to a specific observed mechanism, and enforce the 2h budget (no "Low difficulty / 1.5-4 h"; drop or flag items with feasibleIn2h=false).
